_why_landing_148: Chapter 07 failed its gate twice, both times on LANDING, and both failures were correct. The chapter is a ~5.25s lofted arc (release ~161.15, impact ~166.4); both localizer passes assumed a short flight and pinned LANDING at ~162, which catches the bolt still climbing. The gate's second verdict said so explicitly: 'the strip shows only the bolt still in mid-flight ... the real landing is later'. Rather than spend a third localize run on one chapter, the landing was measured directly from the cached source at 10fps over 165.6-167.8 (scratchpad/f07d_s.png): nothing through 166.0; blue trail entering frame 166.1-166.3; bolt ARRIVES AND STICKS 166.35-166.45; concentric blue sonar sphere peaks 166.7-166.8; scan rays fan out through ~167.2. STAND/AIM/THROW are unchanged and were all explicitly passed by the gate on run w13xd04oo; only LANDING is replaced.
_why_landing_464: Found by a flight-time outlier check across all 30 rows (landing.start - throw.start). cs=464 came out at 0.18s against a next-shortest of 1.85s -- a 10x outlier, and the same shape as the two landings already known wrong. It was wrong for the same reason: the window 472.98-473.45 sits on the author's DRAWN CYAN TRAJECTORY ANNOTATION just after release, not on a deploy. The camera then travels down the corridor following the dart. Measured at 8fps then 20fps: the dart's approach glow runs through ~476.50, and the recon SCAN SWEEP -- blue rays fanning across the wall -- fires 476.60-477.30. New window 476.35-477.35 captures arrival plus the full sweep; flight becomes 3.55s, in line with the other 29 rows.
_why_ability_flips: The localizer reported `recon` on four chapters whose titles carry the author's `(Shocks)` suffix. The hedge was designed so the FOOTAGE decides and the title is only a hint -- so the disagreement was checked against the footage rather than resolved by either label. Full-res peak-landing frames (scratchpad/pk_all.png) put a known recon (cs=148) and a known shock (cs=240) beside all four. The two signatures are unambiguous and completely distinct: RECON = a stuck cylindrical dart body on the surface wrapped in a large DOTTED CONCENTRIC RING sphere, persisting afterwards and followed by fan-out scan rays. SHOCK = a bright pinwheel of curved ELECTRIC ARCS with no dart body, no dotted rings, gone entirely within ~0.5s. All four disputed chapters show the shock pinwheel. Two further independent signals agree: the author's own on-screen captions on these rows describe DAMAGE -- 'killed by this lineup' (637), 'punish attackers' (665), 'kill the B-planter' (687) -- and a recon bolt deals no damage at all; and all 20 non-(Shocks) rows were re-checked the same way (scratchpad/nr_top.png, nr_bot.png) and every one shows the recon signature with captions reading scan/reveal/recon. After these flips, title suffix, caption semantics and landing visual agree on all 30 rows.

_why_seek_vs_exact: The five landings below were pinned with per-frame accurate extraction (one ffmpeg invocation per timestamp, -accurate_seek -ss <t> -frames:v 1), not with an fps= resample after a single input seek. That distinction mattered: the seek-and-resample sheets and the frame-exact sheets disagreed by up to ~0.15s on the same nominal timestamps, which is enough to put a 0.3s shock burst on the wrong side of a window boundary. cs=333 is the case that exposed it -- the resampled sheet placed the first burst at 348.60 and a dark cut at 348.70, the exact sheet placed the same burst at 348.60 but the cut at 348.80. Every window here is quoted from the exact sheet (scratchpad/y_*.png).
_why_landing_batch2: Found by pulling all 30 recut LANDING clips out of storage and watching them as the shipped artifact rather than trusting the gate. Ten came back ambiguous at mid-frame; six-frame strips cleared five of them; the remaining five each turned out to be a real defect of one of two kinds. (a) WINDOW MISSES THE DEPLOY ENTIRELY -- cs=51's window 63.95-65.20 is pure mid-flight; a 5fps sweep of the whole 62.4-68.6 corridor shows one continuous lofted arc from release to a single deploy at 68.55, so the flight really is ~6.5s and the old window sat in the middle of it. (b) WINDOW STRADDLES AN EDITOR CUT OR THE AUTHOR'S DRAWN ANNOTATION -- cs=4 ended at 17.50 exactly as the dart stuck, cs=312 spent its first 0.9s on the drawn blue trajectory ribbon, cs=333 caught its burst then went dark for 0.3s as the camera swung under a roof, and cs=535 spent its last 0.8s panning behind a box after the sweep had ended. None of these is catchable by the adversarial gate: a contact sheet of any of these windows still contains a glowing blue thing somewhere, and the gate never sees the clip as a clip.

excluded.582: The source never puts this lineup's deploy on camera. Swept continuously from the release to the end of the chapter -- 593.3-615.8, at 2-6fps throughout with denser frame-exact passes over 594.4-598.2, 596.0-604.8 and 604.2-607.5 (q_582w/x/y/z.png, y_582/b/c/t.png) -- and there is no recon sphere and no scan sweep anywhere in it. What the chapter actually shows is the release from B at 593.9, then the author WALKING across to A to describe the coverage, then drawing a second dart at 604.9-605.2 that is never followed to its landing. The gate-passed window 604.50-605.60 sits on that second BOW DRAW, which is why it read as a bright blue thing and survived the gate. There is no frame in this source that shows this dart deploying, so no override can fix the row: it is dropped rather than shipped with a landing clip of something else. A second source for Abyss may cover it later.
excluded.219: The source never puts THIS lineup's deploy on camera, and the window that passed the gate is a different dart. Chapter 10 is 'B Lobby to B (Postplant)': the minimap label at 222.80 reads B Lobby and the player icon sits south of the B box, so the stand/aim/throw at 222.1-227.45 are the lineup. Immediately after release the video cuts to the inside of B site and stays there. The dart's own minimap marker (white dart icon plus the cyan scan-radius ring, just south-west of the B box) first appears at 230.10 -- a ~3.0s flight, consistent with the lineup -- but frame-exact sweeps of 227.30-231.00 (y_219a.png, y_219j.png) show the camera indoors on stairs and blank walls the whole time, with no sphere and no scan rays anywhere. The gate-passed window 236.15-236.85 is a SECOND, DIFFERENT throw: at 235.70 the minimap puts the player up at B site, not in B Lobby, and 235.80-236.40 is that dart's release and flight. The only recon sweep visible in the whole chapter runs 238.00-238.30 (peak 238.18, y_219g.png) and belongs to that second dart, whose own body is off the bottom-left edge of frame. 239.00-240.35 has no further sweep before the chapter ends. Shipping 238.0-238.3 would be a landing clip of a dart thrown from somewhere else, so the row is dropped rather than dressed up. A second Abyss source may cover it later.

_why_198_kept: cs=198 was flagged on the all-30 mid-frame sheet as possibly sitting on the bow, the same signature that made cs=582 un-shippable. Frame-exact re-check (y_198a/b/c.png) cleared it: the dart is in flight with a visible blue trail through 212.00, the impact sparkle is at 212.10, the dotted-ring sonar sphere with the stuck dart body runs 212.20-212.40, the scan cone opens at 212.40, and the camera swings into a wall at 212.50. The gate-passed window 211.5-212.45 therefore contains the whole deploy and stops one frame before the swing -- it is the best window the source allows. The bow reads as prominent in every frame only because Sova's bow is his first-person weapon model and is on screen for the entire chapter; bow presence is NOT evidence of a bow-draw defect on its own. No override.
_why_long_flights_kept: The merge's flight-time detector only flags SHORT flights, so the long tail of the distribution was never screened -- and cs=219 proved a long flight is exactly what a cut-away-and-pin-the-wrong-event defect looks like. The four long-flight rows that had never been frame-studied individually were therefore each re-checked frame-exact, and all four are correct: cs=436 'CT to B' (9.95s) is captioned 'this cross-map reveal', so the long flight is the point -- the dart approaches at 456.60-456.80 and sticks inside a full sonar sphere at 457.00 (y_436b.png); cs=240 (6.0s) shows the shock pinwheel at 258.20 (y_240x.png); cs=508 (6.15s) shows the dart plus sphere at 529.65 (y_240x.png frames 7-10); cs=616 (6.1s) shows the shock pinwheel at 632.95 (y_616x.png). cs=616's window runs ~0.4s past the burst into quiet aftermath, which was left alone deliberately: the earlier trims (51, 464, 535) each removed a tail that showed something misleading -- a camera pan-away or a blue wash that hid the geometry -- and a still-readable site is not that. No overrides from this pass.
